'''Tobin Jay Marks''' (born November 25, 1944) is an [[inorganic chemistry]] Professor, the [[Vladimir Nikolayevich Ipatieff|Vladimir N. Ipatieff]] Professor of [[catalysis|Catalytic Chemistry]], Professor of [[Material Science]] and Engineering, Professor of Chemical and Biological Engineering, and Professor of Applied Physics at [[Northwestern University]] in [[Evanston, Illinois]]. Among the themes of his research are synthetic organo-[[Lanthanides|f-element]] and early-transition metal [[organometallic chemistry]], [[polymer chemistry]], [[materials chemistry]], [[Homogeneous catalysis|homogeneous]] and [[heterogeneous catalysis]], molecule-based [[Photonics|photonic]] materials, [[superconductivity]], metal-organic [[chemical vapor deposition]], and biological aspects of transition metal chemistry.

Marks received his [[B.S.]] from the [[University of Maryland]] in 1966 in chemistry, and his [[Ph.D.]] from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1971 under the direction of [[F. A. Cotton]]. He came to Northwestern University in the fall of 1970.

==The Marks Group==

Historically the Marks group has been organized into four teams (A-D), reflecting the historical strengths and the needs of emerging technologies:
* A-team; Organometallics/Catalysis
* B-team: Molecular Photonics
* C-team: Transparent Oxides
* D-team: Molecular Electronics

Marks is known for his ability to tie his efforts to practical problems.  Work in organometallics/catalysis (A-team) has traditionally focused on two main areas: Group IV mediated polymerizations and f-element mediated [[alkene|hydroelementation]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Chen|first1=Eugene Y.X.|last2=Marks|first2=Tobin J.|date=2000|title=Cocatalysts for Metal-Catalyzed Olefin Polymerization: Activators, Activation Processes, and Structure−Activity Relationships|journal= Chemical Reviews |language=en| volume=100|issue=4|pages=1391–1434 |doi=10.1021/cr980462j|pmid=11749269}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hong|first1=Miao|last2=Chen|first2=Eugene Y.X.|date=2017|title=Chemically recyclable polymers: a circular economy approach to sustainability|journal= Green Chemistry |language=en|volume=19|issue=16|pages=3692–3706|doi=10.1039/c7gc01496a}}</ref>  His extensive work in polymerization catalysts and determination of mechanistic traits that allow for optimization, have made these materials and processes industrially relevant.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Nobel Fever is Upon Us|url=https://www.science.org/content/blog-post/nobel-fever-upon-us |access-date=2021-01-11|website=Science (AAAS)|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Chen|first1=Jiazhen|last2=Gao|first2=Yanshan |last3=Marks|first3=Tobin J.|date=2020|title=Early Transition Metal Catalysis for Olefin–Polar Monomer Copolymerization|journal= Angewandte Chemie International Edition |volume=59|issue=35|pages=14726–14735|language=en|doi=10.1002/anie.202000060|pmid=31986236}}</ref>
